Orgs, Auth & Permissions ​

Saidi runs the same code for a single-owner install and a multi-member one. Single-owner is the degenerate case, not a separate product: the tenant context simply resolves to one org with one member.

Tenancy ​

Every request runs inside a tenant context carrying the acting orgId and userId. That context is what makes the storage paths resolve:

memory/global.md                    → local single-user install (userId 'local')
memory/members/<userId>/global.md   → per-member personal memory
memory/projects/<name>.md           → org-scoped
memory/agents/<name>.md             → org-scoped

The local user deliberately keeps the legacy org-root file, so an existing install needs no migration when multi-member support is turned on.

Reflex matching, the fire log, the recent-event feed, and the marketplace catalog are all scoped to the acting org.

Identity ​

ConceptWhere
Tokens & sessionsauth/tokens.ts
OAuthauth/oauth.ts
Orgs & membershipauth/orgs.ts
Channel identitieschannels/identity.ts — maps a Telegram (or other channel) sender to a member

A channel identity is what stops an unlinked Telegram sender from acting as you. Until a sender is linked to a member, it resolves to nobody and gets nothing.

Permissions ​

Permission keys gate what a member may do, independently of what an agent may do.

KeyGrants
runs.viewAllSee every run in the org, not just your own and those shared with you
runs.steerAllSteer any run — reply, pause, resume, approve

Resolution is permissionsFor(member), checked at the tool boundary. A denied call returns a reason (permissionDenied, runActionDenied, agentAccessDenied) rather than failing opaquely.

Run visibility, precisely ​

  • The owner (Run.createdBy) can always view and steer.
  • Members in sharedWith can view the thread but not steer.
  • runs.viewAll sees everything; runs.steerAll can also steer.
  • Every turn and delegation resolves budgets, permissions, and connections against the run's createdBy — not against whoever happens to be watching.

Billing & enforcement ​

Enforcement sits in front of dispatch:

FunctionEffect
usageBlockReasonBlocks the call when the allowance is exhausted, with a reason
clampEffortLowers the effort tier instead of refusing, so a run degrades rather than dies
agentAccessDeniedThe member may not use that agent
permissionDenied / runActionDeniedThe member lacks the permission key
cachedMembershipMembership lookup on the hot path

Spend is recorded per call in the run's usageLog, with unpriced flagged rather than counted as zero — a cap you cannot measure is not a cap.

Invites ​

An org owner invites a member; the invite flow creates the user, attaches membership, and provisions their personal memory file at memory/members/<userId>/global.md. Project and agent memory is not duplicated — it is shared workspace knowledge and stays org-scoped.
